headline: Malcolm Spellman Talks The Drop Direction
post:
Have you been keeping up with the new FX series exploring the rise of West Coast hip-hop? Showrunner Malcolm Spellman recently shared how he shaped the fresh tone for the show. According to The Hollywood Reporter, he admitted that he spent over two years developing the pilot before he "let go" of the original drama to find its true soul.

While audiences often wonder about potential crossover appearances, the creator made it clear that he is “not gonna chase cameos.” Instead, he wants characters to emerge naturally when they fit the narrative.

headline: Jeff Ament's new book captures Pearl Jam's history
post:
Pearl Jam bassist Jeff Ament is opening up about his new photography book, "Since Forever", which collects decades of unseen images of his bandmates according to Rolling Stone. Working alongside his brother Barry, the musician curated candid snapshots capturing the group's journey from their earliest days.

Reflecting on his creative path, Ament shared how working on the movie "Singles" helped restart his photography after he originally sold his camera to move to Seattle. He explained that a chance opportunity on the film's art department provided the tools and funds to finally start shooting again.

While looking back at old memories brought up some stressful times, the project ultimately celebrates the creative bonds of the band. What is your favorite piece of Pearl Jam memorabilia? 📸🎸

#PearlJam #JeffAment #RockHistory
original_title: Jeff Ament on Pearl Jam’s Future — and Why His Band Actually Enjoyed the Nineties
